content:
zane: Heads-up — ran a full nsys + perfetto capture on the 8xA100 pipeline today. Seeing tiny 5–12ms gaps between heavy CUDA kernels and the NCCL all-reduce windows. Feels like microstalls instead of long barriers. Anyone run into this pattern?

ajay: can you paste the nsys command and a small timeline excerpt? also which runtime build / kernel selection commit?

zane: ran: `nsys profile -o /tmp/run1769 --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl -f true --sample=nvtx python -u bench_multi_gpu.py`
zane: timeline snippet (condensed):
```
GPU0: [compute_kernel A] --- 8ms idle --- [ncclAllReduce start]
GPU1: [compute_kernel B] --- 6ms idle --- [ncclAllReduce start]
GPU2: [compute_kernel A] --- 10ms idle --- [ncclAllReduce start]
```
zane: kernels themselves finish at similar times but all-reduce doesn't start until those micro-gaps close. builds: runtime/main@5f3c (kernel-sched-v2 landed last Tuesday). driver: 535.86.

maria: interesting — last week we saw similar jitter but traced it to our KV cache eviction path. a single rank was doing a synchronous checkpoint write which serialized NVLINK for ~8–12ms on the bus and nudged NCCL scheduling. can you grep for any CPU-side blocking in the same window?

zane: i checked CPU stacks in the nsys cpu trace, no fsync or blocking syscall. stack looked like epoll + our batching tier. batching heuristics changed to flush on partial-batch timeout in the v2 scheduler.

ajay: that matches: partial-batch timeout default went from 1ms -> 8ms in the new heuristic. if a slow rank hits partial flush earlier/later it can desync the NVTX annotations we use to align kernels. try setting the batch timeout back to 1ms or force-sync NVTX marks.

olivia: could be NCCL algorithm selection too. when algorithms pick tree vs ring you see different start skew because some ranks enter collective earlier. try `NCCL_ALGO=RING` and `NCCL_COLLNET_DISABLE=1` for a repro run. also enable `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL` to check unexpected reorderings.

zane: ran a short test with `NCCL_ALGO=RING NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` — gaps reduced to 2–4ms but didn't disappear. attaching the nsys stack trace (pasted subset):
```
[GPU -> kernel compute] nvtxRangePush("compute:start")
cudaLaunchKernel(...) // 3.2ms
nvtxRangePop()
--- 3.7ms --- // idle
ncclAllReduce(...) // start after 3.7ms
```
zane: suspect the runtime's kernel selection path may be waiting for all ranks' KV cache lookups to complete before emitting the NVTX end event. that would make NVTX misaligned with actual GPU readiness.

maria: can you instrument the KV path with a dedicated NVTX span that encloses only the CPU lookup and any cache eviction? compare ordering with kernel NVTX. if CPU NVTXs line up with idle windows then it's a KV handshake problem.

ajay: also dump per-rank `nvidia-smi dmon` or `nvtop` timestamps to verify peer DMA activity. if peer-to-peer DMA is stalled that's a HW/driver thing.

perf-bot: automated hint — run `nsys profile --output=timeline_ns --sample=nvtx,cuda,nccl,syscalls` and upload `.qdrep` to /perf/traces for retention.

zane: did the KV NVTX instrument: we see a small CPU NVTX range (2–6ms) that overlaps the GPU idle window. looks like CPU-side cache validation can run after kernel returns but before the NCCL launch path.

olivia: that points at ordering in the runtime host thread. if the host enqueues NCCL too late because it's waiting on a synchronous cache validation, we get the gap. solution: split cache validation into prefetch async path or schedule NCCL launch earlier and provide a compact callback to attach KV results.

ajay: quick mitigations: 1) revert partial-batch timeout to 1ms, 2) set `NCCL_ALGO=RING`, 3) temporarily disable synchronous KV eviction. see if regression disappears.

zane: tried 1+3 together — gaps reduced to noise (<1ms) across 3 runs. seems like a perf regression introduced by combining partial-batch timeout increase + sync KV eviction.

maria: good find. can you file a perf regression ticket referencing run id and attach the nsys .qdrep + small perfetto HTML? tag `@eng-runtime` and `@eng-ml`?

zane: filing now: https://redwood-internal/bugs/PRF-2147 (contains qdrep and sample traces). assigning to @maria for KV changes and @ajay for scheduler rollback.

olivia: long-term: add a NVTX-driven liveness check in the runtime to make NCCL launches resilient to minor host-side ordering chattiness. also add an automated perf-e2e that toggles batch timeout and KV sync flags and compares end-to-end p99 latency.

ajay: i'll open a small revert PR for partial-batch timeout and add a unit test for NVTX alignment.

zane: thanks all — pairing session tomorrow 10am to reproduce and push the fix. :thumbsup:
